: JUDGMENT :

The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB / NH-7 /
CR / 171/2012-13 dated 17.12.2021 pertaining to Sy. No.138 measuring 25 Sq. meters and Sy.
No.139/3B A.P. No.158/2022 measuring 400 Sq. Meters of Yelahanka village, Yelahanka Hobli,
Bengaluru North (Addl) Taluka, Bengaluru Urban District.

.2. The definite case of the petitioner is that the property of respondent No.1 Y.S. Chikkarangappa measuring 25 Sq. meters in Sy. No.138 and 400 Sq. Meters in Sy. No.139/3B of Yelahanka village have been acquired under Preliminary Notification issued by the respondent No.2 under Section 3A(1) vide S.O. No.3159 (E) dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification under Section 3D(1) vide S.O.
No. 1874(E) dated 30.07.2010 and passed the award on 02.04.2011 and awarded a total compensation amount of Rs.3,73,641/- in respect of Sy. No. 138 and Rs. 59,78,256/- in respect of Sy. No.139/3B, which have been received by the respondent No.1(a) and respondent No.3, who are wife and son of claimant No.1 under protest.

Subsequently, on 18.10.2012 the respondent No.1(a)
and respondent No.3 have filed the application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.8,000/- per Sq. feet.
Accordingly, the application is taken by the respondent No.2 for consideration.

.3. Thereafter, the Arbitrator hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ / ARB / NH-7/ CR /
171 /2012-13 dated 17.12.2021.
.4.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting aside the following:

sentences.text:
The petitioner claims that the impugned is liable to be set aside since it is bad in law,
in conflict with public policy of India and patently illegal.
The award suffers from Wednesbury unreasonableness.

Further, The very premise on which the award came to be passed is wholly opposed to the concept of eminent domain and the enhancement as made in the impugn ed award has been awarded without any basis and in a mechanical manner has A.P. No.158/2022 proceeded to enhance the claim.

The Arbitrator considered the circular of the Department of Registration and Stamps bearing No. CVC-19/2010-11 dated 21.09.2011, wherein the compensation amount fixed for agricultural land is Rs.3,000/- per Sq. feet and the said circular is of the year 2011-12, whereas the 3(A) notification was made on 09.12.2009 and therefore, the Arbitrator has failed to consider the market value of the acquired land as on the date of notification under Section 3(A) of the Act.

The SLAO and CA, Hebbal has fixed the compensation amount as per the award dated 02.04.2011 based on the guidance value and market value as prescribed by the Sub-Registrar, Bengaluru North for the period between 08.12.2008 and 09.12.2009 i.e., Rs. 1389/- per Sq. feet as well as through perusal of sale deeds of other lands located near the acquired land, but the Arbitrator failed to take this aspect into consideration while passing the impugned award and A.P. No.158/2022 contrary to the provisions of the Section 3-G(7) of the NH Act.
The award of 10% of the compensation award under Section 3-G(2) of the NH Act is contrary to the provisions of the NH Act.
The impugned Arbitral Award is against the well settled law of fixation of compensation and the public Exchequer should not be put to undue burden by excess valuation.

That no findings are given by the Arbitrator in exercise of his jurisdiction under Section 3G(5) of the NH Act, in determining the market value based on the use/category of the land as on the date of acquisition, which alone can be taken into account.
That the cause of action for this petition arose on 17.12.2021, when the Arbitral Award was passed within the jurisdiction of this Court.
The petition is filed within the period of limitation as extended by the Hon'ble Supreme Court and among other grounds, prayed for relief claimed in the petition.

The respondents 1(a) and 3 filed detailed objections to the above petition and claimed that the acquired land is attached to the Bengaluru International Airport road, Yelahanka and it is situated on the NH-7 and have commercial potential and the same has been acquired for commercial purpose.

The said land is nearer too and close by the Bengaluru City and abutting the existing National Highways, surrounded by several commercial establishment such as residential layouts, Hotel industries, convention halls, banks, petrol bunks, lodges, shops, vehicle service stations and residential houses, hospitals, nursing homes, villas and industries, star hotels, IT and BT companies and also big industries like Bisleri mineral water company and Ozone urban township (Largest Township in Bengaluru) Shobha lifestyle villas, Shobha lifestyle legacy, colleges, schools and business park and aero SEZ.
Hardware and software parks etc.,
and his property is nearby Bengaluru International Airport at Devanahalli, several multinational companies have already invested and A.P. No.158/2022 establishments.
The area being fast growing area wherein the land value is more than Rs. 10,000/- per Sq. feet.
The KIADB also acquired various lands for development of Industries and also further extension of Airport Development.

.7. The above application is supported with the affidavit of petitioner, wherein, it is stated that the petitioner received copy of the award dated 17.12.2021 with a direction to pay the enhanced amount to the respondent No.1 in claim No.LAQ / ARB / NH-07 / CR / 171 / 2012-13.

Further, during pandemic there was a change in the post for Project Director and the post A.P. No.158/2022 remained vacant for several months and he has succeeded the post of Project Director of the applicant.
Further in the month of February and March 2022, several employees of the applicant tested positive for Covid-19 and the office was completely non-functional.

Due to the aforesaid reasons, the concerned department of their office could not co-ordinate with their legal counsel to pass instructions and further to furnish relevant records to challenge the order passed by respondent No.2.
Hence, there is a delay of 29 days in filing the above petition is bonafide reason but not intentional.
Among other grounds prayed for condonation of delay if any in filing the petition.

.13. Point No.2:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The respondents 1(a) and 3 are the owners of the property bearing Sy. No.138 measuring to an extent of 25 Sq. Meters of Yelahanka village and the property bearing Sy. No. 139/3B measuring to an extent of 400 Sq.
Meters of Yelahanka village and the said properties have been acquired for widening of NH-7 under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 30.07.2010, is an admitted fact.

It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the respondent No.2 has enhanced the compensation from Rs.1,389/-
per Sq. feets to Rs.
4200/- per Sq. feet.

It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.
3,73,641/- and Rs.59,78,256/-
A.P. No.158/2022 were disbursed to the respondent No. 1(a) and respondent No.3 as compensation.

.14. Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the respondent No. 1(a) and respondent No.3 filed an application before the respondent No.2 claiming that he is entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs. 8,000/- per Sq.
feet as on 18.10.2012.

On the basis of said application, the respondent No. 2 hold an inquiry and passed an order in LAQ / ARB / NH-7 / CR / 171 / 2012-13 dated 17.12.2021.
.15.
The said enhancement has been challenged by the petitioner in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent No.2 without considering the relevant provisions of NHA Act and also without considering the guidance value or market value of the property as on the date of Preliminary Notification enhanced the compensation by relying on the guidance value of the year 2009 published vide notification bearing No. CVC-19/2010-11 dated 21.09.2011 and the A.P.
No.158/2022 said document is not part of arbitration proceedings.
The petitioner also claimed the Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009.

As such, the respondent No.2 ought to have considered the market value of the land of the year 2009 and not of the year 2011 as the aforesaid notification relied by the Arbitrator came to effect from 2011 i.e., after lapse of more than a year from the date of publication of Preliminary Notification.
Accordingly claimed that the said enhancement cannot be accepted.
It is true that as per the NH Act, the market value of the land as on the date of Preliminary Notification has to be considered.

.16. The petitioner also claimed that whatever the document relied by the respondent No.2 for enhancing the compensation is not brought to the notice of the petitioner before passing the award/judgment.
Accordingly, claimed that such award is liable to be set aside as per Section 24 of National Highways Authority Act.

In this context, the petitioner relied on the decision reported in (2019) 15 SCC 131 in a case of Ssangyong A.P. No.158/2022 Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs. National Highways Authority of India.

Supreme Court held that whatever the document relied by the Arbitrator shall be brought to the notice of the parties, so that the parties can make submission or give a rebuttal evidence about such documents.
However, in the case on hand, such notification is not found in the record received from the Arbitrator.

In the case on hand, the Arbitrator has enhanced compensation to Rs. 3000/- per square feet for agricultural land and 40% towards industrial purposes, totally to Rs. 4,200/- per Sq.
feet from Rs.1,389/- per square feet on the basis notification subsequent to the preliminary notification as aforesaid.

As discussed earlier, the preliminary notification is dated 09.12.2009 and the Arbitrator relied on the notification bearing No.CVC/19/2010-11 dated 21-09- 2011 and the said notification itself is published subsequent to the award passed by the LAO.
The LAO/respondent No.3 passed the award as on A.P. No.158/2022 02.04.2011.
Whatever the enhancement has been granted by the Arbitrator, certainly effect the State or State Exchequer.
Hence, Arbitrator shall give reasons for enhancement of the compensation.

As already stated above, the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 has not given any explanation for enhancement except relying on the notification bearing No.CVC/19/2010-11 dated 21.09.2011, which is not the part of arbitration proceedings and the same is not brought to the notice of petitioner before passing the award.
Hence such enhancement cannot be accepted.

.17. Apart from that it is stated in the operative portion of the order that the respondent No. 2 has increased 40% towards industrial purpose by using his discretion but how the said discretion has been used or what is the basis for using the said discretion is nowhere explained in the order.

The arbitrator is expected to give some reasons for the enhancement of 40% or under what circumstances, the respondent No.1(a) and 3 are entitle for said 40% enhancement to A.P.
No.158/2022 be explained or reasoned by the Arbitrator, otherwise such discretion cannot be accepted as discretion has to be used or exercised judiciously.

.18. In the case on hand, though the respondent No.2 served with the notice, appeared before the Court through DGP, but not resisted the case of the petitioner or to support the award passed by the respondent No.2.
Absolutely there is no material placed before the court to disbelieve the petitioner case or to substantiate the award passed by the respondent No.2.
Hence, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to intervene with the award passed by the Arbitrator and the award is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, the point No.2 is held in the affirmative.
.19. Point No.3:
In view of my above finding, I proceed to pass the following.
A.P. No.158/2022 ORDER IA filed by the petitioner to condone the delay in filing the petition is allowed.
Petition filed under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is hereby allowed.

Consequently, the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 in case No. LAQ / ARB / NH-7 / CR / 171/ 2012- 13 dated 17.12.2021 pertaining to Sy. No.138 measuring 25 Sq. Meters and Sy.
No.139/3B measuring 400 Sq. Meters of Yelahanka village, is hereby set aside with a liberty to the parties to pursue their remedy in accordance with law.
